8.en: Inquisitors see the Imperium from an incomparable vantage, burdened with unique scope, power, and freedom of thought. Their duty is to no system, sector, or segmentum, but to the God-Emperor’s domain as a whole. They serve no master save Him on Terra. Their freedom to interpret their duty places them beyond the hold of the Lex Imperialis and Imperial Creed, holding doubts and philosophies that any ordinary citizen would be condemned for. These few souls, who know the true breadth of horrors that threaten to choke the Imperium, bear a duty to become horrors themselves, for in the salvation of the Imperium, there is no deed beyond their limits, no cost counted in Human lives that is deemed too high. Billions of souls have been condemned on the orders of the Inquisition, for innocence is never enough for a soul to be spared.

12.en: In their scope and jurisdiction, the only souls of equal standing to an Inquisitor are others of their creed. Inquisitors primarily work alone, typically only coming together to face the direst threats. To the citizens of the Imperium, Inquisitors are so far removed from their everyday lives that they are made near-mythic through their distance and holy duties — terrors lurking in the darkness to some, little more than tall tales to most. Inquisitors act with the full sanction and authority of the God-Emperor; they are His eyes in the darkest corners of the Imperium and His instrument of justice and punishment. To the people of @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.VeiDfnkV55kTAkRw]{Kallastin}, a world that felt the sting of their presence in the Macharian Heresy, Inquisitors are remembered as the lurking death of the apostate, the God-Emperor’s wrath and tyranny manifest.

16.en: This chapter provides advice and inspiration for GMs portraying Inquisitor Patrons in their games. How to build their mythology and relationships with their acolyte characters and portray them as the utterly terrifying and world-shaking characters they truly are. Additionally, there is mechanical advice about setting up briefings and debriefings with your players' characters, how they should they be treated in moments of loyalty and betrayal, and how GMs and players alike should handle the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40]{Inquisitor’s Rosette} as a defining piece of equipment.

26.en: This Chapter contain a roster of sample Inquisitor Patrons, who are also the leading personalities of @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W]{Chapter V: The Heresies Macharia }. These can be used as pre-made Patrons during character creation or as allied or opposed characters in your campaigns. Take note of their secrets, but do not share them with your players. Note each one’s Future Boons & Liabilities Table, which suggests additional upgrades and downgrades that can affect players and Patrons alike when they reach story milestones.
